edition.name: 2026 Review of Particle Physics rho-meson listings
edition.citation: F. Takahashi et al. (Particle Data Group), Int. J. Mod. Phys. A 41, 2630011 (2026)

conventions.name: mass representation
conventions.value: PDG listed mass; rho(770)^0 uses the listed Breit-Wigner mass
conventions.rationale: The comparison must not mix pole and Breit-Wigner conventions silently.

conventions.name: default radial assignment
conventions.value: rho(770)^0 is the anchor; rho(1450) and rho(1700) are candidate radial excitations
conventions.rationale: The default reproduces a common phenomenological assignment but does not treat either excited-state label as exact.

conventions.name: rho(1570) sensitivity alternative
conventions.value: rho(1570) is recorded as an excluded, ambiguous alternative for model mode n=2
conventions.rationale: PDG lists rho(1570) but omits it from the Summary Table and notes that it may be an OZI-violating decay mode of rho(1700), so it cannot be assumed to be an independent radial state.

conventions.name: comparison observable
conventions.rationale: Ratios remove the one dimensionful scale from each bottom-up construction.

conventions.name: source covariance
conventions.value: Listed mass uncertainties are treated as mutually independent before ratio normalization
conventions.rationale: The frozen PDG listings do not provide a covariance matrix; the shared denominator correlation is then generated explicitly by the ratio Jacobian.

entries.label: rho(770)^0
entries.notes: Neutral-state Breit-Wigner mass used as the shared ratio denominator.

entries.label: rho(1450)
entries.notes: Included as a candidate first radial excitation. PDG calls this estimate an educated guess, and the model assignment is not a validation claim.

entries.label: rho(1570)

uncertainty.combination: Components are retained separately because this excluded entry is not used in the default covariance calculation.

entries.notes: Considered as an alternative n=2 assignment but excluded from the default comparison: PDG omits rho(1570) from the Summary Table and states that it may be an OZI-violating decay mode of rho(1700).

entries.label: rho(1700)
entries.source_locator: rho(1700) MASS, eta rho0 and pi+ pi- modes, OUR ESTIMATE
entries.notes: Included in the owner-approved default scenario as a candidate second radial excitation; this phenomenological assignment is not a validation claim.

transformations.description: Normalize every included mass to the rho(770)^0 anchor.
transformations.uncertainty_propagation: Use the Jacobian of all ratios with respect to the independent listed masses so the shared m_0 uncertainty generates off-diagonal covariance.
